title: Consistent windowed quotas for embedding + rerank fanout with granular refund protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We currently have inconsistent quota and billing behavior for non-chat endpoints that fan out (embeddings + separate rerank/score calls + optional function/tool calls). Customers see over-charge cases when: (1) client retries or speculative callers trigger duplicate calls within short windows, (2) partial successes occur (some fanout branches succeed, others fail), or (3) a long-running rerank triggers a delayed response that crosses quota windows. This ticket scopes a design and implementation to ensure consistent windowed quota accounting with an explicit granular refund protocol for partial/duplicate charges.
background_and_context: Existing system records discrete charge events per RPC (charge_event) with a timestamp and token_count. Quota enforcement uses a per-customer rolling window counter that sums token_count by minute buckets.

Failure modes observed in customer reports and internal QA: duplicate charge events when clients retry on timeouts; speculative prefetch flows where server-initiated prefetch and client requests both bill; partial fanout where embedding succeeds but downstream rerank/toolcall fails leading to disputed charges.

Previous tickets covered reconciliation and partial-charge refunds but focused on embeddings-only or tool-invocation-only paths; we need a unified approach covering multi-call fanout (embed -> rerank -> toolcall/structured output).

Business impact: customers reported overbilling and occasional quota exhaustion causing application outages (medium-high severity for enterprise customers). We must reduce incidents and provide deterministic guarantees for refunds/credits within SLA.
Related existing artifacts: design doc 'billing-reconcile-2025' (Confluence), PR #5421 (billing events v2 schema), dashboard 'quota-window-drifts' (Grafana).
This ticket will change charge semantics and needs coordination with product (billing policy), support (customer messaging), and infra (DB migration).
goals: Define an explicit windowed coalescing strategy so multiple related calls within a short causal window are consolidated for quota enforcement where policy permits (e.g., speculative prefetch dedup).
Introduce an idempotent charge atom (charge_atom_id) and causal metadata that allow deterministic reconciliation and refunds without double-counting.
Add a granular refund protocol for partial fanout failures that produces stable final accounting within 24h and supports automated credits for customers.
Minimize latency/regression to normal request path (<5% p50 extra latency) and keep storage growth for charge metadata bounded.
Expose observability: per-charge lineage, reconciled vs provisional charge states, refund triggers and counts on the console dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Charge events emitted for embed/rerank/toolcall include charge_atom_id, dedup_key (optional), causal_parent_ids, and consumption_window_id.
Quota aggregation code uses consumption_window_id + coalesce(dedup_key, charge_atom_id) to prevent double counting across retries within the configured coalescing window.
Refund protocol runs automatically for partial failures and creates 'credit' events visible in usage APIs and billing exports within 24 hours.
No customer-facing change in API surface; debug-only headers (X-Redwood-Charge-Atom) available for support tracing.
Unit and integration tests covering: retry dedup, partial fanout, speculative prefetch coalescing, long-running crossing-window case, and migration scenarios.
design_notes: Charge atom model: every customer-facing RPC generates a provisional 'charge atom' if it will consume billable tokens. Charge atoms have: id, request_signature_hash, dedup_key (optional client-supplied idempotency key), causal_parents (list of upstream charge_atom_ids), provisional_token_estimate, final_token_count (filled on completion).
Coalescing window: default 60s sliding window per customer for speculative/preemptible dedup. This is configurable per-customer via account profile.
Quota counting: only 'committed' charge atoms are summed for quota; provisional atoms may reserve soft capacity but are not final until final_token_count is set or a timeout triggers reconciliation.

Refund protocol: when fanout completes with fewer final_token_count than the provisional sum, the reconciler emits a 'credit' event tied to the original charge_atom_id(s). Credits have metadata mapping to the original invoice line for traceability.

Idempotency and retries: dedup_key and request_signature_hash are used to collapse client retries; server-side speculative prefetch uses causal_parent to link generated prefetch atoms to eventual client requests to avoid double-billing.

Long-running crossing-window flows: attach consumption_window_id to charge atom at creation (based on request_time truncated to window length) but allow reconciler to migrate final_token_count across windows for correct billing while ensuring quota enforcement uses coalesced view.
Storage: charge atoms stored in a compact time-series table with TTL 90d. Reconciler job is incremental and marks atoms as FINAL or CANCELED (with reason).
Privacy/compliance: no additional PII stored; ensure KMS/HSM keys used for signing dedup tokens when required by enterprise contracts.
implementation_plan: Schema: add charge_atom fields to billing_events table (charge_atom_id, dedup_key, causal_parents, provisional_token_estimate, final_token_count, consumption_window_id). See PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789.
API layer: emit provisional charge atom at RPC entry and return X-Redwood-Charge-Atom header. Minimal path change; lightweight. (ENG work: runtime + api-proxy).

Quota service: update monthly/minute window aggregation to use consumption_window_id + deduping rules. Backwards compatible: existing events without charge_atom_id treated as pre-v2 and counted in legacy pipeline.
Reconciler: implement a distributed reconciler (kafka->worker) that finalizes provisional atoms after completion or timeout, emits credits for negative deltas, and writes final_token_count.
Refund/credit ledger: extend billing ledger to accept 'credit' events referencing charge_atom_ids for traceability; exportable to billing CSV and console.
Testing: unit tests in billing service; integration tests simulating retry storms, partial fanout failures, and crossing-window completion using staged traffic in canary environment.
Docs & support: write KB article on how refunds are issued and add debug guidance for Support.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable charge_atom v2 for 10% of traffic for internal and low-risk customers. Monitor reconciliation rates and false-positive refunds. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 50% with feature flag; enable in-console tracing and customer debug headers. (1 week)
Phase 3 (full): flip default for new customers; offer opt-in for existing until migration window ends. (2 weeks)
Communication: notify billing customers in advance (Support + Account teams) and provide opt-out for first billing cycle after migration.
Fallback: if reconciler causes regressions, a kill-switch disables provisional charges and reverts to legacy counting for affected customers.
monitoring_and_alerting: Grafana dashboard: 'charge_atom_reconciliation' showing provisional vs final token delta histogram, credits emitted per hour, and top customers by refunds.
Alert: >1% of total tokens for a customer turned into credits within a 24h window (P0).
Alert: reconciler lag >10m for >5k provisional atoms (P1).
Support logs: expose charge_atom lineage traces via internal trace tool (link in related_links).
migration_steps: Backfill: run a one-time migration to mark recent 7d events without charge_atom_id as legacy; not required to backfill older data.
Dual-write: billing producer writes both legacy billing_event and new charge_atom references during canary to validate downstream consumers.
Data retention: ensure charge_atom table TTL and houseclean scripts are in place before full rollout.
Customer opt-in: provide flag in account profile to enable conservative dedup (no coalescing) for customers who want strict counted-per-RPC behavior.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: mis-coalescing could undercount tokens leading to revenue loss. Mitigation: conservative default (coalescing only when dedup_key or causal_parent detected) and monitoring alerting on credits percentage.
Risk: added latency from provisional bookkeeping. Mitigation: emit provisional atom asynchronously and avoid blocking RPC on durable write; fall back to synchronous path in failure cases.
Risk: migration complexity and billing disputes. Mitigation: clear support runbook, visible reconciliation trace IDs for customers, and delayed full-enablement with opt-out window.
